paragraphs.text: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?
paragraphs.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; ἐπιμένωμεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, ἵνα ἡ χάρις πλεονάσῃ;
paragraphs.translit: Ti oun eroumen; epimenōmen tē hamartia, hina hē charis pleonasē;

paragraphs.text: God forbid. We who died to sin, how shall we any longer live therein?
paragraphs.original: μὴ γένοιτο· οἵτινες ἀπεθάνομεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, πῶς ἔτι ζήσομεν ἐν αὐτῇ;
paragraphs.translit: mē genoito· hoitines apethanomen tē hamartia, pōs eti zēsomen en autē;

paragraphs.text: Or are ye ignorant that all we who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?
paragraphs.original: ἢ ἀγνοεῖτε ὅτι ὅσοι ἐβαπτίσθημεν εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν εἰς τὸν θάνατον αὐτοῦ ἐβαπτίσθημεν;
paragraphs.translit: ē agnoeite hoti hosoi ebaptisthēmen eis Christon Iēsoun eis ton thanaton autou ebaptisthēmen;

paragraphs.text: We were buried therefore with him through baptism unto death: that like as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.
paragraphs.original: συνετάφημεν οὖν αὐτῷ διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος εἰς τὸν θάνατον, ἵνα ὥσπερ ἠγέρθη Χριστὸς ἐκ νεκρῶν διὰ τῆς δόξης τοῦ πατρός, οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐν καινότητι ζωῆς περιπατήσωμεν.
paragraphs.translit: synetaphēmen oun autō dia tou baptismatos eis ton thanaton, hina hōsper ēgerthē Christos ek nekrōn dia tēs doxēs tou patros, houtōs kai hēmeis en kainotēti zōēs peripatēsōmen.

paragraphs.text: For if we have become united with [him] in the likeness of his death, we shall be also [in the likeness] of his resurrection;
paragraphs.original: Εἰ γὰρ σύμφυτοι γεγόναμεν τῷ ὁμοιώματι τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἐσόμεθα·
paragraphs.translit: Ei gar symphytoi gegonamen tō homoiōmati tou thanatou autou, alla kai tēs anastaseōs esometha·

paragraphs.text: knowing this, that our old man was crucified with [him], that the body of sin might be done away, that so we should no longer be in bondage to sin;
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο γινώσκοντες ὅτι ὁ παλαιὸς ἡμῶν ἄνθρωπος συνεσταυρώθη, ἵνα καταργηθῇ τὸ σῶμα τῆς ἁμαρτίας, τοῦ μηκέτι δουλεύειν ἡμᾶς τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ,
paragraphs.translit: touto ginōskontes hoti ho palaios hēmōn anthrōpos synestaurōthē, hina katargēthē to sōma tēs hamartias, tou mēketi douleuein hēmas tē hamartia,

paragraphs.text: for he that hath died is justified from sin.
paragraphs.original: ὁ γὰρ ἀποθανὼν δεδικαίωται ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας.
paragraphs.translit: ho gar apothanōn dedikaiōtai apo tēs hamartias.

paragraphs.text: But if we died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him;
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ ἀπεθάνομεν σὺν Χριστῷ, πιστεύομεν ὅτι καὶ συζήσομεν αὐτῷ·
paragraphs.translit: ei de apethanomen syn Christō, pisteuomen hoti kai syzēsomen autō·

paragraphs.text: knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death no more hath dominion over him.
paragraphs.original: εἰδότες ὅτι Χριστὸς ἐγερθεὶς ἐκ νεκρῶν οὐκέτι ἀποθνῄσκει, θάνατος αὐτοῦ οὐκέτι κυριεύει·
paragraphs.translit: eidotes hoti Christos egertheis ek nekrōn ouketi apothnēskei, thanatos autou ouketi kyrieuei·

paragraphs.text: For the death that he died, he died unto sin once: but the life that he liveth, he liveth unto God.
paragraphs.original: ὃ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν, τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀπέθανεν ἐφάπαξ· ὃ δὲ ζῇ, ζῇ τῷ θεῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ho gar apethanen, tē hamartia apethanen ephapax· ho de zē, zē tō theō.

paragraphs.text: Even so reckon ye also yourselves to be dead unto sin, but alive unto God in Christ Jesus.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς λογίζεσθε ἑαυτοὺς εἶναι νεκροὺς μὲν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ζῶντας δὲ τῷ θεῷ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs kai hymeis logizesthe heautous einai nekrous men tē hamartia zōntas de tō theō en Christō Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey the lusts thereof:
paragraphs.original: Μὴ οὖν βασιλευέτω ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θνητῷ ὑμῶν σώματι εἰς τὸ ὑπακούειν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: Mē oun basileuetō hē hamartia en tō thnētō hymōn sōmati eis to hypakouein tais epithymiais autou,

paragraphs.text: neither present your members unto sin [as] instruments of unrighteousness; but present yourselves unto God, as alive from the dead, and your members [as] instruments of righteousness unto God.
paragraphs.original: μηδὲ παριστάνετε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα ἀδικίας τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, ἀλλὰ παραστήσατε ἑαυτοὺς τῷ θεῷ ὡσεὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ζῶντας καὶ τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα δικαιοσύνης τῷ θεῷ.
paragraphs.translit: mēde paristanete ta melē hymōn hopla adikias tē hamartia, alla parastēsate heautous tō theō hōsei ek nekrōn zōntas kai ta melē hymōn hopla dikaiosynēs tō theō.

paragraphs.text: For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under law, but under grace.
paragraphs.original: ἁμαρτία γὰρ ὑμῶν οὐ κυριεύσει, οὐ γάρ ἐστε ὑπὸ νόμον ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ χάριν.
paragraphs.translit: hamartia gar hymōn ou kyrieusei, ou gar este hypo nomon alla hypo charin.

paragraphs.text: What then? shall we sin, because we are not under law, but under grace? God forbid.
paragraphs.original: Τί οὖν; ἁμαρτήσωμεν ὅτι οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑπὸ νόμον ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ χάριν; μὴ γένοιτο·
paragraphs.translit: Ti oun; hamartēsōmen hoti ouk esmen hypo nomon alla hypo charin; mē genoito·

paragraphs.text: Know ye not, that to whom ye present yourselves [as] servants unto obedience, his servants ye are whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?
paragraphs.original: οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ᾧ παριστάνετε ἑαυτοὺς δούλους εἰς ὑπακοήν, δοῦλοί ἐστε ᾧ ὑπακούετε, ἤτοι ἁμαρτίας εἰς θάνατον ἢ ὑπακοῆς εἰς δικαιοσύνην;
paragraphs.translit: ouk oidate hoti hō paristanete heautous doulous eis hypakoēn, douloi este hō hypakouete, ētoi hamartias eis thanaton ē hypakoēs eis dikaiosynēn;

paragraphs.text: But thanks be to God, that, whereas ye were servants of sin, ye became obedient from the heart to that form of teaching whereunto ye were delivered;
paragraphs.original: χάρις δὲ τῷ θεῷ ὅτι ἦτε δοῦλοι τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὑπηκούσατε δὲ ἐκ καρδίας εἰς ὃν παρεδόθητε τύπον διδαχῆς,
paragraphs.translit: charis de tō theō hoti ēte douloi tēs hamartias hypēkousate de ek kardias eis hon paredothēte typon didachēs,

paragraphs.text: and being made free from sin, ye became servants of righteousness.
paragraphs.original: ἐλευθερωθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἐδουλώθητε τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ·
paragraphs.translit: eleutherōthentes de apo tēs hamartias edoulōthēte tē dikaiosynē·

paragraphs.text: I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity of your flesh: for as ye presented your members [as] servants to uncleanness and to iniquity unto iniquity, even so now present your members [as] servants to righteousness unto sanctification.
paragraphs.original: ἀνθρώπινον λέγω διὰ τὴν ἀσθένειαν τῆς σαρκὸς ὑμῶν· ὥσπερ γὰρ παρεστήσατε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν δοῦλα τῇ ἀκαθαρσίᾳ καὶ τῇ ἀνομίᾳ εἰς τὴν ἀνομίαν, οὕτως νῦν παραστήσατε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν δοῦλα τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ εἰς ἁγιασμόν.
paragraphs.translit: anthrōpinon legō dia tēn astheneian tēs sarkos hymōn· hōsper gar parestēsate ta melē hymōn doula tē akatharsia kai tē anomia eis tēn anomian, houtōs nyn parastēsate ta melē hymōn doula tē dikaiosynē eis hagiasmon.

paragraphs.text: For when ye were servants of sin, ye were free in regard of righteousness.
paragraphs.original: Ὅτε γὰρ δοῦλοι ἦτε τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ἐλεύθεροι ἦτε τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ.
paragraphs.translit: Hote gar douloi ēte tēs hamartias, eleutheroi ēte tē dikaiosynē.

paragraphs.text: What fruit then had ye at that time in the things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death.
paragraphs.original: τίνα οὖν καρπὸν εἴχετε τότε ἐφʼ οἷς νῦν ἐπαισχύνεσθε; τὸ γὰρ τέλος ἐκείνων θάνατος·
paragraphs.translit: tina oun karpon eichete tote ephʼ hois nyn epaischynesthe; to gar telos ekeinōn thanatos·

paragraphs.text: But now being made free from sin and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto sanctification, and the end eternal life.
paragraphs.original: νυνὶ δέ, ἐλευθερωθέντες ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας δουλωθέντες δὲ τῷ θεῷ, ἔχετε τὸν καρπὸν ὑμῶν εἰς ἁγιασμόν, τὸ δὲ τέλος ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
paragraphs.translit: nyni de, eleutherōthentes apo tēs hamartias doulōthentes de tō theō, echete ton karpon hymōn eis hagiasmon, to de telos zōēn aiōnion.

paragraphs.text: For the wages of sin is death; but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
paragraphs.original: τὰ γὰρ ὀψώνια τῆς ἁμαρτίας θάνατος, τὸ δὲ χάρισμα τοῦ θεοῦ ζωὴ αἰώνιος ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ta gar opsōnia tēs hamartias thanatos, to de charisma tou theou zōē aiōnios en Christō Iēsou tō kyriō hēmōn.
